    def run_bibtex(
        command: tuple[str, ...],
        bib_text: str,
        style_text: str,
        cites: list[str] | str,
        tmp_path: Path,
        *,
        timeout: int = 30,
        expect_exit: int = 0,
        with_log: bool = False,
        aux_text: str | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any] | None]:
        """Run bibtex with a bib, a style, and cites (or aux). Returns (bbl_text,
        log_dict_or_None). Asserts exit code."""
        bib_file = tmp_path / "refs.bib"
        bst_file = tmp_path / "style.bst"
        output_file = tmp_path / "out.bbl"
        log_file = tmp_path / "out.log" if with_log else None
        # Multiple probes may share tmp_path; stale artifacts must not let an
        # invocation that writes nothing inherit an earlier invocation's credit.
        output_file.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        if log_file is not None:
            log_file.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        bib_file.write_text(bib_text, encoding="utf-8")
        bst_file.write_text(style_text, encoding="utf-8")
    
        args: list[str] = [
            *command,
            "--bib",
            str(bib_file),
            "--style",
            str(bst_file),
            "--output",
            str(output_file),
        ]
        if aux_text is not None:
            aux_file = tmp_path / "paper.aux"
            aux_file.write_text(aux_text, encoding="utf-8")
            args += ["--aux", str(aux_file)]
        if cites or aux_text is None:
            cites_file = tmp_path / "cites.txt"
            cites_text = cites if isinstance(cites, str) else "\n".join(cites) + "\n"
            cites_file.write_text(cites_text, encoding="utf-8")
            args += ["--cites", str(cites_file)]
        if log_file is not None:
            args += ["--log", str(log_file)]
    
        result = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)

editorial.last_message: Completed the Python BibTeX implementation; unchanged source passes 380/386 under 1.2.4. Remaining gaps concern MACRO namespaces, predefined-name declarations, whitespace flushing and past-end name selection. Independent historic-binary parity was explicitly left unverified during generation.
editorial.notes: Official BibTeX 1.2.4 regrade: 381/386 under 1.2.3 becomes 380/386. The single changed observation is positive past-end format.name$ selection: the supplied WEB and 20 independent native-oracle probes retain the final scanned name, correcting the previous empty-result expectation. All 386 official outcome values match the frozen independently checked candidate; all 385 other node outcomes are exactly unchanged from 1.2.3. The changed score removes one false failure for Astra JavaScript and one false-credit point for each other submission; the correction follows supplied source authority and is applied consistently. No warning-kind, message, count or absence is imposed for the unmapped native diagnostic. Publicly permitted no-op top$, inter-token spaces, brace-width and quoted-unknown-warning choices remain accepted. All 8 canonical style integrations pass. Remaining failed observations are clustered below rather than presented as independent bug counts. Database MACRO declarations enter the executable symbol table, wrongly rejecting a macro named crossref and wrongly allowing a macro-only name as an executable BST function. These are two observations of one shared namespace conflation. The loader explicitly bypasses duplicate checking when ENTRY redeclares the predefined crossref field. The supplied WEB inserts ENTRY names into the existing function namespace and rejects this redeclaration. OutputBuffer.newline preserves trailing spaces and emits all-space lines. The supplied WEB trims trailing whitespace and suppresses a nonempty buffer made empty by trimming. The summary ordinary description conflicts but explicitly gives WEB precedence; it is not an allowed approximation. Two failures share this flush behavior. format_name returns empty when a positive index exceeds the list length. Supplied WEB and 20 independent local oracle probes instead retain the final scanned name; corrected 1.2.4 removes the former false credit. No warning kind, format, count or absence is imposed. Original full transcript/source reviews are retained below with exact path, hash, reviewer and payload; their prior tool-accounting claims are historical and superseded by the current session audit. Current session-based v2 tool count is 45 (originally recorded 45); proven corrections preserve the definition. Every input/output/cache/reasoning count and cost field is preserved; tokens remain complete and adapter reparse agrees. The original result bytes, generation metadata, source manifest and original score remain unchanged. Official audit source/hash, frozen test bytes and raw-score parsing all validate. Regrading makes no model calls and adds no generation cost. Run conditions: apps explicitly disabled in the recorded launch; no external tool invocation observed.
